expectations.text: Describes the §127.12 VSD process: prompt initial notification to DDTC, thorough internal investigation, then a full report with facts, causes, remediation
expectations.evidence: "Voluntary Self-Disclosure (VSD) under 22 CFR § 127.12": Step 1 initial notification to DDTC, Step 2 internal investigation, Step 3 final report with "factual narrative... root-cause analysis... corrective actions".

expectations.text: States VSD is a significant mitigating factor and can result in no penalty, warning letter, or reduced civil penalty
expectations.evidence: "it is the strongest mitigating factor available"; outcome "ranging from no action or a warning letter up to a civil penalty (typically reduced given VSD credit)".

expectations.text: Cites current penalty exposure: civil penalties up to ~$1.37M per violation (annually adjusted) and criminal exposure up to $1M/20 years per violation
expectations.evidence: No penalty figures anywhere — neither the ~$1.37M civil per-violation maximum nor the $1M/20-year criminal exposure is cited.

expectations.text: Advises immediate steps: stop the violating activity, preserve records, consider disclosure counsel, review for related EAR/OFAC issues
expectations.evidence: Preserve records ("litigation hold") and counsel are advised, but never says to STOP the violating activity, and no review for related EAR/OFAC exposure.

expectations.text: Mentions submissions run through DDTC's DECCS platform (which deployed its Data Collection Modernization release in September 2026)
expectations.evidence: DECCS platform and the September 2026 Data Collection Modernization release are never mentioned.
